    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersWashington half-smoke sausages with chilliGrilled half-pork, half-beef smoked sausages in buns with beef chilli and mustardHow to make it300g beef mince2 onions2 tsp chilli powder200g crushed tomatoes125ml water4 smoked half-pork half-beef sausages4 hot dog buns4 tbsp yellow mustardFinely chop the onions, keeping half aside raw for serving.Simmer the mince with the onion, chilli powder, tomatoes and water, stirring now and then, until thick.Split the sausages and grill until browned and hot.Serve in the buns with the chilli, mustard and the raw chopped onion.Brooklyn smoked salmon bagel bitesMini bagels with dill cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers and red onionHow to make it12 mini bagels200g cream cheese1 lemon1 tbsp chopped dill1/4 tsp salt200g smoked salmon1 red onion1 tbsp caperscracked black pepper, to tasteSplit the bagels and toast until golden.Mix the cream cheese with the lemon zest, dill and salt.Spread thickly on each bagel half, then top with folds of smoked salmon, thin rings of red onion and a few capers.Finish with pepper and a little more dill.Sam's safe house pancakes and baconSam letting Steve and Natasha lie low at his houseHow to make itAs written, serves 4Small fluffy buttermilk pancakes stacked with melting butter and maple syrup, with crisp streaky bacon on the side.Whisk 300g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 eggs, 400ml buttermilk and 30g melted butter into a thick batter.Fry 4 tbsp at a time in a buttered pan over medium heat for 2 minutes a side until golden, making about 16.Keep warm in a low oven.Fry 12 bacon rashers until crisp.Stack the pancakes with a knob of butter and pour over maple syrup.Fried green tomatoes with buttermilk ranchOn your left. Sam always gets the last one.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsThai basil chicken over riceStir-fried chicken with garlic, chilli and Thai basil over jasmine rice, crisp fried eggHow to make it600g chicken thigh fillets, minced or finely chopped6 garlic cloves, crushed3 red chillies, chopped2 tbsp fish sauce1 tsp sugar1 cup Thai basil leaves300g jasmine rice4 eggsRinse the rice and cook it, then keep warm.Stir-fry the chicken with the garlic and red chillies in a hot wok until cooked through.Add the fish sauce and sugar, then toss through the Thai basil.Fry the eggs in hot oil until the edges are crisp.Serve the chicken over rice with a fried egg on top.Helicarrier beef and red wine stewThe S.H.I.E.L.D. helicarriers rising out of the PotomacHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef chuck braised for hours in red wine and stock with carrots, onions and potatoes until spoon tender, served with crusty bread.Toss 1.2kg diced beef chuck in 2 tbsp plain flour and brown in batches in oil.Soften 2 diced onions and 2 garlic cloves, then add the beef, 250ml red wine, 500ml beef stock, 2 tbsp tomato paste and 2 bay leaves.Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours.Add 3 chopped carrots and 500g potato chunks and cook 1 hour more.Season and serve with crusty bread.SweetsShield pieCherry and blueberry pie with a woven lattice top, served warm with ice creamHow to make it400g frozen cherries200g blueberries100g caster sugar3 tbsp cornflour3 sheets of shortcrust pastry1 egg, beaten for glazing1 L vanilla ice creamToss the cherries and blueberries with the sugar and cornflour.Line a pie dish with pastry, add the fruit and weave a lattice top from strips of pastry. Brush with egg.Bake at 190°C until golden and bubbling.Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.DrinksSmithsonian cherry lime phosphateCherry syrup, lime juice and bitters over crushed ice, topped with sodaHow to make it300g frozen pitted cherries150g caster sugar150ml water60ml lime juice4 dashes of bitters800ml soda water1 bag crushed ice4 lime wedgesSimmer the cherries with the sugar and water, then mash well.Strain and cool the syrup completely.Fill tall glasses with crushed ice and add the cherry syrup, lime juice and bitters to each.Top with soda water, stir once and garnish with a cherry and a lime wedge.Fresh mint iced teaTrouble Man on the record player. Sam's pick.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
